title: No longer writing or reading much, saving his eyes
summary: He has stopped writing his book and letters and reading to save his failing eyesight, though he can still read a newspaper.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Well now, here you are at home, and it's difficult for you to get around, and if you're not going out to a job, how do you spend your time, mostly?
Even Now I thought you were going to say why don't you practice in. That's what I was going to --
Oh, I wouldn't lecture you, Herman. No sir.

No, I mean -- no, but you're right. Because I get interested in fooling around with something else. I used to write, and a little music here, and try to start my -- writing my book, writing my book. And I've had some -- right now I haven't written a lot in so damn long, man, I don't even write my brothers, or nobody. You know.
Well, with your eyes and everything, it's kind of hard to write.
It is, yeah. Yeah. When I stopped reading -- I used to do a little reading here and there, and
I stopped. I said well, I'll save my eyesight for music only, you know, one of those things. And then well, it panned out pretty good.

But now, as bad as my eyes are, when I go to see -- go to my doctors, they say well, they can't -- well, Mr. Autrey, we can't give you glasses now. We're going to wait a little while longer. I say well look, I can pick up a newspaper, I can read a newspaper. I can -- I don't wear any glasses. Well, I can't read everything, but I can read enough to know that -- you know.
But this is just one of those things.
